text: Come along, little seed. Hills catch the rain. Water shapes a home. And one day, a forest grows. Let us follow the clues.
First, raise the noise frequency. Broad hills become smaller ridges. The seed stays the same.
More samples reveal the same landscape in finer detail.
Now raise the snow line. The mountain stays still; only its coat changes.
Give the same hills more rain. Water carries soil downhill, cutting some slopes and leaving sediment below.
Add moisture to the same land. The habitat map changes, opening different homes for life.
Inside the mountain, density tells us where solid ground exists.
Widen the tunnel. A cave opens. Then add a pillar after cutting: the order changes what remains.
Carve one small pocket. Only nearby chunks need rebuilding; the distant landscape stays cached.
Finer voxels cost more work.
Smaller chunks change that tradeoff.
Marching Cubes finds the surface.
Turn the vector field. The same particles follow a new direction, revealing the invisible wind.
In this fluid study, dye follows the flow. Pressure correction reduces divergence. Watch the two versions side by side.
Repeat a branching rule. A simple line becomes a tree, one generation at a time.
Open the angle; spread the crown.
With births switched off, trees grow larger, not more numerous.
Now allow new seeds. The same starting forest becomes a growing population.
Crowding changes who can thrive.
Here comes the tide. Follow the waterline as it climbs. A low path floods, and the route must change. As water retreats, the shore returns.
A little world, shaped by connected questions. Land, water, and life. These studies remain separate models. The next story begins with the rule you choose.
